newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish narrowly mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished narrowly mixed, as most contracts consolidated Monday's sharp losses and traders started squaring positions ahead of the U.S. September employment data on Friday, analysts said.
"People are waiting around for Friday's numbers," one currency trader said.
December yen drifted to the upside, but found little momentum as the dollar/yen traded inside Monday's range.
"We see today's action as healthy and indicative of new highs in the not-too-distant future being established for the U.S. dollar," Dennis Gartman wrote in the Gartman Letter.
Gartman, who is editor and publisher of the Gartman Letter, sees no reason to change his outlook for the U.S. dollar, which has been bullish since April 1995.

"I would say the strength in the U.S. dollar is incumbent on the strength of the U.S. economy," Gartman said, adding that signs that the U.S.'s labor market was growing would fuel the next spike higher in the U.S. dollar.

He believes that the U.S. will continue its strong-dollar policy after the U.S. Presidential elections, contrary to some market concerns that the U.S. may abandon its dollar policy once the elections are out of the way.
"There is a greater propensity in an election year to weaken the dollar to mollify the auto companies," Gartman said.

December yen remained below the GLOBEX high of $0.009120, as the U.S. dollar hovered around the 111.30 level for most of the day. Some traders said the dollar/yen's upside may be limited at 112.00, or $0.009025 in December yen, in the near-term due to a barrier option at that level.
December marks and Swiss francs traded in even more narrow ranges, while Canadian dollar futures extended their earlier gains.
December Canadian dollars rallied to $0.7378, through the two-month high at $0.7371 and through resistance at $0.7372.

Gartman said the trend towards more fiscally-responsible government in the provinces, coupled with the last of the debt roll-over for six months and Canada's rising trade surplus, will continue to lift Canadian dollars.

He is looking for spot Canadian dollars to fall to 1.3250, which is near its 2-1/2 year low set at 1.3276, in the next several months. December Canadian dollars set their contract high at $0.7460 on October 6, 1995.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was off $0.000005 at $0.009071, marks off $0.0003 at $0.6587, Swiss francs up $0.0001 at $0.8040, sterling off $0.0006 at $1.5640, Canadian dollars up $0.0010 at $0.7376, Australian dollars up $0.0013 at $0.7902 and Mexican pesos up $0.000675 at $0.127175.
